_about: Plain-language text for the contract-stack page (scripts/contract-stack.mjs). The facts come from the repository: states, addresses, line counts and gas. This file only words them for a reader new to the project. A finding's text has one variant per state (open, fixed, accepted); when the variant for its current state is missing, the page shows the review's own title and status instead, so a state change never leaves stale wording.

contracts.HoldbackRules: The referee. It checks every signed message and deadline, and is the only thing that tells the vault to pay, refund or hold.
contracts.HoldbackBonds: The adjudicators' security deposits. Each deal locks part of a deposit until its appeal window closes, and an overturned decision is paid from it.
contracts.HoldbackTypes: The shapes of the signed messages, hashed exactly as Crow's off-chain code signs them.
contracts.DrandQuicknetBeacon: The public dice roll. It checks drand's signature on a random value, which picks the fallback's and the appeal's AI judges.
contracts.IHoldbackBeacon: The interface every beacon implements, so the rules contract can use the real one on Sepolia and a test one locally.
contracts.SimBeacon: A test beacon for the local chain only. It is never deployed to a public network.

H-1.title: A judge could re-roll its own panel
H-1.fixed: A fallback or appeal adjudicator could retry the dice roll that picks its AI judges by changing one number in its decision. Every decision is now bound to the delivery round it judges.

H-2.title: A refunded buyer could also get the work
H-2.fixed: A decision could release the decryption key on a deal that ended in a refund, so the buyer kept both the money and the work. The key now travels only with a payment to the seller.

M-1.title: A buyer's direct reclaim could freeze bonds
M-1.fixed: If the buyer took the money straight back from the vault, the adjudicators' deposits for that deal stayed locked. They are now freed.

M-2.title: A late delivery could block a refund
M-2.fixed: A delivery arriving after its deadline could still count and beat the buyer's refund. The deadline is now checked on every path.

M-3.title: A fake deal could lock a backup judge's deposit
M-3.fixed: Anyone could name a backup or appeal adjudicator in a sham deal and tie up its bond. A backup's bond is now locked only when it actually takes the case.

L-1.title: A decision could be paired with another delivery
L-1.open: A judge's decision names the delivery round, not the exact delivery, so a seller who signed two versions could settle a decision about one with the other.
L-1.fixed: A judge's decision named the delivery round, not the exact delivery, so a seller who signed two versions could settle a decision about one with the other. Decisions and early accepts now name the exact delivery, the contract keeps the one that landed and refuses any other, and the judge checks the seller's signature on what it judges.

L-2.title: The deposit vault trusts the amount it is told
L-2.open: With a token that charges a fee on each transfer, the vault would record more than it received. The fix checks the balance actually received, as the escrow vault already does.

L-3.title: An appeal can be filed with no deposit
L-3.open: Now that winning an appeal pays out, a free appeal is a free shot at the price. A minimum appeal deposit, set in the deal's terms, must be in place before any real money.
L-3.accepted: An appeal can be filed with no deposit. Accepted until the appeal rules move on chain.

L-4.title: The primary judge's seed check is shorter than it could be
L-4.open: The primary judge's commitment to its random seed is checked on 144 bits and is not tied to the deal. The fix ties it to the deal.

L-5.title: The appeal judge stakes no deposit of its own
L-5.open: An appeal judge with nothing at stake can move the price out of the first judge's deposit. Until it carries its own bond, the first judge protects itself by accepting only appeal judges it trusts.

L-6.title: The vault's expiry ignores the judging deadline
L-6.open: If the judging deadline falls after the vault's expiry, an on-time decision could not be paid. The fix derives the expiry from every deadline, or refuses such terms at funding.

L-7.title: The winner could block the loser's appeal
L-7.open: Either party could file the deal's only appeal, so the party a decision favoured could take the slot with a free appeal.
L-7.fixed: Only the party the decision went against may appeal now, so the winner cannot take the deal's one appeal slot and block the loser.

L-8.title: A deadline already past can reveal the fallback's dice roll
L-8.open: If the judging deadline has already passed when a deal is funded, the fallback's random value is public before anyone signs. The fix refuses such a deal at funding.

I-2.title: A fee branch that never pays
I-2.open: The mutual-settlement fee share is a constant zero, so one branch of code never runs. The fix removes that dead code.

I-8.title: Winning an appeal paid nothing
I-8.open: When an appeal overturns a decision, nobody is paid from the judge's deposit, so the wronged party wins the record but not the money.
I-8.fixed: When an appeal overturned a decision, nobody was paid from the judge's deposit. Now the first judge's deposit pays the wronged party the full price.

gas.label: A normal deal: fund, deliver, accept
The work fails its checks: refund
Nothing delivered: the buyer takes the money back
One of Crow's servers is offline
The AI judges disagree: the appeal judge decides
The judge goes silent: the fallback decides
